Sign changes grid detected refined uniroot. slope refined root estimated finite difference (step size 0.01) classify proper anomalous. selected proper crossing stored cut score pair.

title: Find TIF-Crossing Cut Scores for MST Routing — find_cut
text: run_mst internally orders candidate modules ascending module index maps routing rank 1 lowest-index module. cut-score routing assign low-theta examinees easiest module, modules stage must numbered ascending difficulty order (easiest module = lowest index). find_cut() checks assumption issues warning difficulty order match index order. Regardless warning, cut scores always computed consecutive module pairs supplied index order (e.g., modules 2 & 3 3 & 4, 2 & 4 4 & 3). returned cut scores within stage sorted ascending order, required cut.

title: Find TIF-Crossing Cut Scores for MST Routing — find_cut
code: ## -- Setup: use the built-in simMST 1-3-3 panel -------------------------- ## simMST is a 7-module, 3-stage MST panel (8 dichotomous 3PLM items each). ## Modules 1 (routing), 2-4 (stage 2: easy/medium/hard), ##         5-7 (stage 3: easy/medium/hard). x         <- simMST$item_bank module    <- simMST$module route_map <- simMST$route_map  ## -- Find TIF-crossing cut scores ----------------------------------------- ## For each adjacent module pair at stages 2 and 3, find_cut() identifies ## the theta at which the harder module's TIF first exceeds the easier ## module's TIF (proper crossing), and returns it as a cut score. cut_result <- find_cut(x = x, module = module, route_map = route_map) #> Warning: Stage 2: difficulty order of modules does not match their index order. #>   Ascending index order    : modules 2, 3, 4 #>   Ascending difficulty order: modules 2, 4, 3 (mean locations: -0.731, 0.128, 0.134) #>   run_mst() routes by ascending module index (rank 1 -> lowest index). #>   If index order differs from difficulty order, cut-score routing may #>   not produce the intended module assignments. #>   Consider redesigning the panel so that easier modules have lower indices. #> Warning: Stage 2, pair (module 2 vs module 3): 2 proper crossings found at theta = [-0.3955, 3.0936]. #> Selecting the crossing closest to ref_theta = 0.0000: theta = -0.3955. #> To override the selection, specify a different 'ref_theta'.  ## Print a summary: crossing points found, anomalous crossings excluded, ## and the final selected cut scores per stage transition. print(cut_result) #> MST TIF-Crossing Cut Score Results #> ================================================== #>  #> stage.2 #> ----------------------------------- #>   Modules (index order)    : 2, 3, 4 #>   Modules (difficulty order): 2, 4, 3 #>   Mean item locations      : -0.7313, 0.1342, 0.1279 #>   Selected cut score(s)    : -0.3955, 0.4423 #>   Pair details: #>     [mod2_vs_mod3] #>       Proper crossing(s)    : 2  [theta = -0.3955, 3.0936] #>       Anomalous crossing(s) : 1  [theta = 2.1328]  (excluded) #>       Selected cut score    : -0.3955 #>     [mod3_vs_mod4] #>       Proper crossing(s)    : 1  [theta = 0.4423] #>       Anomalous crossing(s) : 2  [theta = -1.3914, 5.7208]  (excluded) #>       Selected cut score    : 0.4423 #>  #> stage.3 #> ----------------------------------- #>   Modules (index order)    : 5, 6, 7 #>   Modules (difficulty order): 5, 6, 7 #>   Mean item locations      : -0.8563, -0.1402, 0.4899 #>   Selected cut score(s)    : -0.6612, 0.5131 #>   Pair details: #>     [mod5_vs_mod6] #>       Proper crossing(s)    : 1  [theta = -0.6612] #>       Selected cut score    : -0.6612 #>     [mod6_vs_mod7] #>       Proper crossing(s)    : 1  [theta = 0.5131] #>       Anomalous crossing(s) : 1  [theta = -1.7322]  (excluded) #>       Selected cut score    : 0.5131 #> ================================================== #> Usage: run_mst(..., route_method = NULL, cut_score = <result>$cut_score)  ## -- Visualise TIF curves and cut scores --------------------------------- ## plot() shows TIF curves for every module faceted by stage. ## Selected cut scores appear as solid black vertical lines with theta ## labels at the crossing point. Anomalous crossings (if any) appear ## as dashed red lines. plot(cut_result)                         # stages stacked vertically (default)  plot(cut_result, layout = "horizontal")  # stages side by side  plot(cut_result, show_anomalous = FALSE) # hide anomalous crossing markers   ## Inspect the cut_score element -- a list directly compatible with run_mst() ## cut_score[[1]]: two cut scores for the stage-1 -> stage-2 transition ## cut_score[[2]]: cut scores for the stage-2 -> stage-3 transition cut_result$cut_score #> $stage.2 #> [1] -0.3954894  0.4422831 #>  #> $stage.3 #> [1] -0.6611766  0.5130904 #>   ## Compare with the manually specified cut scores stored in simMST simMST$cut_score #> [[1]] #> [1] -0.3954891  0.4422893 #>  #> [[2]] #> [1] -0.6611704  0.5130905 #>   ## -- Use the cut scores in run_mst() -------------------------------------- ## Pass cut_result$cut_score directly to run_mst() with route_method = NULL. ## This replaces pure MFI routing with TIF-crossing-based fixed cut scores, ## preventing anomalous path reversals at the extremes of the theta scale. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ set.seed(1) theta_true <- rnorm(500) result <- run_mst(   x            = x,   route_map    = route_map,   module       = module,   theta        = theta_true,   route_method = NULL,   cut_score    = cut_result$cut_score ) } # }

title: irtQ: Unidimensional Item Response Theory Modeling — irtQ-package
text: irtQ package provides tools fitting unidimensional item response theory (IRT) models test data include dichotomous polytomous items. enables calibration pretest item parameters, estimation examinees' abilities, offers comprehensive suite utilities unidimensional IRT analysis, including model-data fit evaluation, differential item functioning (DIF) detection, . item parameter estimation, package employs marginal maximum likelihood estimation via expectation-maximization (MMLE-EM) algorithm (Bock & Aitkin, 1981). calibrate pretest (newly developed) items, supports fixed item parameter calibration (FIPC; Kim, 2006) fixed ability parameter calibration (FAPC; Ban et al., 2001; Stocking, 1988), also known Stocking’s Method . addition, package offers multiple-group item calibration via MMLE-EM algorithm. ability estimation, several widely used scoring methods available, including: Maximum likelihood estimation (ML) Maximum likelihood estimation fences (MLF; Han, 2016) Weighted likelihood estimation (WL; Warm, 1989) Maximum posteriori estimation (MAP; Hambleton et al., 1991) Expected posteriori estimation (EAP; Bock & Mislevy, 1982) EAP summed scoring (Thissen et al., 1995; Thissen & Orlando, 2001) Inverse test characteristic curve (TCC) scoring (e.g., Kolen & Brennan, 2004; Kolen & Tong, 2010; Stocking, 1996) addition, package offers variety utilities IRT analysis, including: Evaluating model-data fit Detecting DIF Computing classification accuracy consistency indices Importing item ability parameters popular IRT software Running flexMIRT (Cai, 2017) directly R Simulating response data Computing conditional distribution observed scores using Lord-Wingersky recursion Calculating item test information characteristic functions Visualizing item test characteristic information curves Supporting additional tools flexible practical IRT analyses

title: irtQ: Unidimensional Item Response Theory Modeling — irtQ-package
text: irtQ package supports dichotomous polytomous item response theory (IRT) models. dichotomous items, one-, two-, three-parameter logistic models (1PLM, 2PLM, 3PLM) available. polytomous items, graded response model (GRM) (generalized) partial credit model (GPCM) implemented. fitting partial credit model (PCM), note item discrimination (slope) parameters fixed 1. following, let \(Y\) response examinee latent ability \(\theta\) item, suppose polytomous item \(K\) unique score categories. IRT 1–3PL models IRT 1PLM, 2PLM, 3PLM models, probability examinee ability \(\theta\) responds correctly item given : $$P(Y = 1 \mid \theta) = g + \frac{(1 - g)}{1 + \exp(-Da(\theta - b))},$$ \(\) item discrimination (slope) parameter, \(b\) item difficulty parameter, \(g\) guessing parameter. constant \(D\) scaling factor used make logistic function approximate normal ogive function, typically set \(D = 1.702\). 1PLM used, discrimination parameter \(\) either fixed constant value (e.g., \(= 1\)) constrained equal across items. 1PLM 2PLM models, guessing parameter fixed \(g = 0\). GRM graded response model (GRM), probability examinee latent ability \(\theta\) responds score category \(k\) (\(k = 0, 1, \ldots, K - 1\)) given : $$P(Y = k \mid \theta) = P^{*}(Y \ge k \mid \theta) - P^{*}(Y \ge k + 1 \mid \theta),$$ $$P^{*}(Y \ge k \mid \theta) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-Da(\theta - b_{k}))},$$ $$P^{*}(Y \ge k + 1 \mid \theta) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-Da(\theta - b_{k+1}))},$$ \(P^{*}(Y \ge k \mid \theta)\) cumulative probability (category boundary function) score category \(k\), functional form similar 2PL model. parameter \(b_{k}\) represents difficulty (threshold) parameter associated  boundary categories \(k - 1\) \(k\). Note probability responding lowest highest score category can written : $$P(Y = 0 \mid \theta) = 1 - P^{*}(Y \ge 1 \mid \theta),$$ $$P(Y = K - 1 \mid \theta) = P^{*}(Y \ge K - 1 \mid \theta).$$ GPCM generalized partial credit model (GPCM), probability examinee latent ability \(\theta\) responds score category \(k\) (\(k = 0, 1, \ldots, K - 1\)) given : $$       P(Y = k \mid \theta) =       \frac{\exp\left(\sum_{v = 0}^{k} Da(\theta - b_v)\right)}       {\sum_{h = 0}^{K - 1} \exp\left(\sum_{v = 0}^{h} Da(\theta - b_v)\right)},     $$ \(b_v\) threshold (step) parameter associated category boundary \(v\) item. alternative parameterizations, \(b_v\) can expressed \(b_v = \beta - \tau_v\), \(\beta\) overall location (difficulty) parameter item, \(\tau_v\) threshold score category \(v\). irtQ package, item \(K\) unique score categories requires \(K - 1\) threshold parameters, \(b_0 = 0\) fixed convention thus \(\sum_{v=0}^{0} Da(\theta - b_v) = 0\) lowest category. fitting partial credit model, item discrimination parameter \(\) fixed 1.

what: Item Calibration for a Linear Test Form
title: irtQ: Unidimensional Item Response Theory Modeling — irtQ-package
text: Item parameter estimation linear test form can performed using est_irt() function, implements marginal maximum likelihood estimation via expectation-maximization (MMLE-EM) algorithm (Bock & Aitkin, 1981). function returns item parameter estimates along standard errors, computed using cross-product approximation method (Meilijson, 1989). irtQ package supports calibration mixed-format tests containing dichotomous polytomous items. also provides flexible set options address various practical calibration needs. example, users can: Specify prior distributions item parameters Fix specific parameters (e.g., guessing parameter 3PL model) Estimate latent ability distribution using nonparametric histogram method (Woods, 2007) irtQ package, item calibration linear test form typically involves two main steps: Prepare examinees' response data set linear test form estimate item parameters using est_irt() function, response data set linear test form must first prepared. data provided either matrix data frame format, rows represent examinees columns represent items. missing responses, properly coded (e.g., NA). Estimate item parameters using est_irt() function estimate item parameters, several key input arguments must specified est_irt() function: data: matrix data frame containing examinees' item responses. model: character vector specifying IRT model item (e.g., "1PLM", "2PLM", "3PLM", "GRM", "GPCM"). cats: numeric vector indicating number score categories item. dichotomous items, use 2. D: scaling constant (typically 1.702) align logistic function normal ogive model. Optionally, may incorporate prior distributions item parameters: use.aprior, use.bprior, use.gprior: Logical indicators specifying whether apply prior distributions discrimination (), difficulty (b), guessing (g) parameters, respectively. aprior, bprior, gprior: Lists specifying distributional form corresponding parameters prior. Supported distributions include Beta, Log-normal, Normal. response data contain missing values, must specify missing value code via missing argument. default, latent ability distribution assumed follow standard normal distribution (.e., N(0, 1)). However, users can estimate empirical histogram latent distribution setting EmpHist = TRUE, based nonparametric method proposed Woods (2007).

what: Pretest Item Calibration with the Fixed Ability Parameter Calibration (FAPC) Method (e.g., Stocking, 1988)
title: irtQ: Unidimensional Item Response Theory Modeling — irtQ-package
text: computerized adaptive testing (CAT), fixed ability parameter calibration (FAPC) method—also known Stocking’s Method (Stocking, 1988)—one simplest straightforward approaches calibrating pretest items. involves estimating item parameters using maximum likelihood estimation, conditional known estimated proficiency values. FAPC primarily used place parameter estimates pretest items onto scale operational item parameters. can also used recalibrate operational items evaluating potential item parameter drift (Chen & Wang, 2016; Stocking, 1988). method known produce accurate unbiased item parameter estimates items randomly administered examinees, rather adaptively, often case pretest items (Ban et al., 2001; Chen & Wang, 2016). irtQ package, FAPC can conducted two main steps: Prepare data set containing item response data corresponding ability (proficiency) estimates. use est_item() function, two input data sets required: Ability estimates: numeric vector containing examinees' ability (proficiency) estimates. Item response data: matrix data frame containing item responses, rows represent examinees columns represent items. order examinees response data must exactly match order ability estimates. title: irtQ: Unidimensional Item Response Theory Modeling — irtQ-package
text: examples demonstrate estimate item parameters linear test form, calibrate pretest items using FIPC FAPC methods. examples use simulated data sets, examinees' response data generated based true item parameters true ability values using simdat() function. examples utilize item parameter estimates imported flexMIRT output file sample, includes mixed-format test 55 items: 50 dichotomous items modeled 3PLM 5 polytomous items modeled GRM. item parameters treated "true" values data generation. Specifically: Items 1–38: 3PLM items Items 39–40: GRM items Items 41–52: 3PLM items Items 53–55: GRM items (5 score categories) Example 1 – Estimating item parameters linear test form example uses first 40 items (38 3PLM 2 GRM) form linear test. test assumed administered reference group 2,000 examinees whose latent ability follows standard normal distribution, N(0, 1). Examples 2 3 – Calibrating pretest items using FIPC FAPC examples assume new test form consisting 55 items described . first 40 items treated fixed operational items (.e., Example 1), remaining 15 items newly developed pretest items calibrated. new test form administered separate group 2,000 examinees, whose ability distribution assumed follow N(0.5, 1.3²). calibration pretest items conducted scale old form using FIPC FAPC procedures, respectively.
code: # Attach the packages library(irtQ)  ##--------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## 1. Item parameter estimation for a linear test form ##---------------------------------------------------------------------------  ## Step 1: Prepare response data for the reference group ## Import the "-prm.txt" output file from flexMIRT meta_true <- system.file("extdata", "flexmirt_sample-prm.txt", package = "irtQ")  # Extract item metadata using `irtQ::bring.flexmirt()` # This will serve as the base test form for later pretest item examples x_new <- irtQ::bring.flexmirt(file = meta_true, "par")$Group1$full_df  # Extract items 1 to 40 to define the linear test form used in this illustration x_ref <- x_new[1:40, ]  # Generate true ability values (N = 2,000) from N(0, 1) for the reference group set.seed(20) theta_ref <- rnorm(2000, mean = 0, sd = 1)  # Simulate response data for the linear test form # Scaling factor D = 1 assumes a logistic IRT model data_ref <- irtQ::simdat(x = x_ref, theta = theta_ref, D = 1)  ## Step 2: Estimate item parameters for the linear test form mod_ref <- irtQ::est_irt(   data       = data_ref,                              # Response data   D          = 1,                                     # Scaling factor   model      = c(rep("3PLM", 38), rep("GRM", 2)),     # Item models   cats       = c(rep(2, 38), rep(5, 2)),              # Score categories per item   item.id    = paste0("Ref_I", 1:40),                 # Item IDs   use.gprior = TRUE,                                  # Use prior for guessing parameter   gprior     = list(dist = "beta", params = c(5, 16)),# Prior: Beta(5,16) for g   Quadrature = c(49, 6),                              # 49 quadrature points from -6 to 6   group.mean = 0,   group.var  = 1,                                     # Fixed latent ability: N(0,1)   EmpHist    = TRUE,                                  # Estimate empirical ability distribution   Etol       = 1e-3,                                  # E-step convergence tolerance   MaxE       = 500)                                   # Max EM iterations  # Summarize estimation results irtQ::summary(mod_ref)  # Extract item parameter estimates est_ref <- mod_ref$par.est print(est_ref)  ##------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 2. Pretest item calibration using Fixed Item Parameter Calibration (FIPC) ##------------------------------------------------------------------------------  ## Step 1: Prepare item metadata for both fixed operational items and pretest items # Define anchor item positions (items to be fixed) fixed_pos <- c(1:40)  # Specify IDs, models, and categories for 15 pretest items # Includes 12 3PLM and 3 GRM items (each GRM has 5 categories) new_ids <- paste0("New_I", 1:15) new_models <- c(rep("3PLM", 12), rep("GRM", 3)) new_cats <- c(rep(2, 12), rep(5, 3))  # Construct item metadata using `shape_df_fipc()`. See Details of `shape_df_fipc()` # for more information # First 40 items are anchor items (fixed); last 15 are pretest (freely estimated) meta_fipc <- irtQ::shape_df_fipc(x = est_ref, fix.loc = fixed_pos, item.id = new_ids,                                  cats = new_cats, model = new_models)  ## Step 2: Prepare response data for the new test form # Generate latent abilities for 2,000 new examinees from N(0.5, 1.3²) set.seed(21) theta_new <- rnorm(2000, mean = 0.5, sd = 1.3)  # Simulate response data using true item parameters and true abilities data_new <- irtQ::simdat(x = x_new, theta = theta_new, D = 1)  ## Step 3: Calibrate pretest items using FIPC # Fit 3PLM to dichotomous and GRM to polytomous items # Fix first 40 items and freely estimate the remaining 15 pretest items mod_fipc <- irtQ::est_irt(   x           = meta_fipc,                     # Combined item metadata   data        = data_new,                      # Response data   D           = 1,                             # Scaling constant   use.gprior  = TRUE,                          # Use prior for guessing parameter   gprior      = list(dist = "beta", params = c(5, 16)),  # Prior: Beta(5,16) for g   Quadrature  = c(49, 6),                      # 49 quadrature points from -6 to 6   EmpHist     = TRUE,                          # Estimate empirical ability distribution   Etol        = 1e-3,                          # E-step convergence tolerance   MaxE        = 500,                           # Max EM iterations   fipc        = TRUE,                          # Enable FIPC   fipc.method = "MEM",                         # Use Multiple EM cycles   fix.loc     = c(1:40))                       # Anchor item positions to fix  # Summarize estimation results irtQ::summary(mod_fipc)  # Extract item parameter estimates est_new_fipc <- mod_fipc$par.est print(est_new_fipc)  # Plot estimated empirical distribution of ability emphist <- irtQ::getirt(mod_fipc, what="weights") plot(emphist$weight ~ emphist$theta, xlab="Theta", ylab="Density", type = "h")   ##------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 3. Pretest item calibration using Fixed Ability Parameter Calibration (FAPC) ##------------------------------------------------------------------------------  ## Step 1: Prepare response data and ability estimates # In FAPC, ability estimates are assumed known and fixed. # Estimate abilities for new examinees using the first 40 fixed operational (anchor) items only. # Pretest items are not used for scoring, as their parameters are not yet calibrated.  # Estimate abilities using ML method via `irtQ::est_score()` # Based on fixed anchor item parameters and corresponding responses score_ml <- irtQ::est_score(   x      = est_ref,            # Metadata with operational item parameters   data   = data_new[, 1:40],   # Responses to anchor items   D      = 1,                  # Scaling constant   method = "ML",               # Scoring method: Maximum Likelihood   range  = c(-5, 5))           # Scoring bounds  # Extract estimated abilities theta_est <- score_ml$est.theta  ## Step 2: Calibrate pretest items using FAPC # Only the 15 pretest items are included in the calibration mod_fapc <- irtQ::est_item(   data       = data_new[, 41:55],                      # Responses to pretest items   score      = theta_est,                              # Fixed ability estimates   D          = 1,                                       # Scaling constant   model      = c(rep("3PLM", 12), rep("GRM", 3)),       # Item models   cats       = c(rep(2, 12), rep(5, 3)),                # Score categories   item.id    = paste0("New_I", 1:15),                   # Item IDs   use.gprior = TRUE,                                    # Use prior for guessing parameter   gprior     = list(dist = "beta", params = c(5, 16))   # Prior: Beta(5,16) for g )  # Summarize estimation results irtQ::summary(mod_fapc)  # Extract item parameter estimates est_new_fapc <- mod_fapc$par.est print(est_new_fapc)

title: Pseudo-count D2 method — pcd2
text: function calculates Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistic evaluate item parameter drift, described Cappaert et al. (2018) Stone (2000). Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistic designed detect item parameter drift efficiently without requiring item recalibration, making especially valuable computerized adaptive testing (CAT) environments. method compares observed expected response frequencies across quadrature points, represent latent ability levels. expected frequencies computed using posterior distribution examinee's ability (Stone, 2000), providing robust sensitive measure item parameter drift, ensuring stability accuracy test time.

title: Pseudo-count D2 method — pcd2
code: pcd2(   x,   data,   D = 1,   item.skip = NULL,   missing = NA,   Quadrature = c(49, 6),   weights = NULL,   group.mean = 0,   group.var = 1,   crit.val = NULL,   min.resp = NULL,   purify = FALSE,   max.iter = 10,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Pseudo-count D2 method — pcd2
text: x data frame containing item metadata (e.g., item parameters, number categories, IRT model types, etc.). See est_irt() simdat() details item metadata. data frame can easily created using shape_df() function. data matrix examinees' item responses corresponding items specified x argument. Rows represent examinees columns represent items. D scaling constant used IRT models make logistic function closely approximate normal ogive function. value 1.7 commonly used purpose. Default 1. item.skip numeric vector item indices exclude IPD analysis. NULL, items included. Useful omitting specific items based prior insights. missing value indicating missing responses data set. Default NA. Quadrature numeric vector length two: first element: number quadrature points second element: symmetric bound (absolute value) points example, c(49, 6) specifies 49 evenly spaced points –6 6. points used E-step EM algorithm. Default c(49,   6). weights two-column matrix data frame containing quadrature points (first column) corresponding weights (second column) latent variable prior distribution. NULL, scale latent ability distribution fixed match scale provided quadrature points weights. weights points can conveniently generated using function gen.weight(). NULL, normal prior density used instead, based information provided Quadrature, group.mean, group.var arguments. Default NULL. group.mean numeric value specifying mean latent variable prior distribution weights = NULL. Default 0. value fixed resolve indeterminacy item parameter scale calibration. group.var positive numeric value specifying variance latent variable prior distribution weights = NULL. Default 1. value fixed resolve indeterminacy item parameter scale calibration. crit.val critical value applied hypothesis testing using Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistic. Default NULL. min.resp positive integer specifying minimum required number responses evaluated item. Defaults NULL. purify Logical. Indicates whether apply purification procedure. Default FALSE. max.iter positive integer specifying maximum number iterations allowed purification process. Default 10. verbose Logical. TRUE, progress messages purification procedure displayed; FALSE, messages suppressed. Default TRUE.

title: Pseudo-count D2 method — pcd2
text: function returns list containing four main components: no_purify list containing results Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) analysis without applying purification procedure. includes: ipd_stat data frame summarizing Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistics items. columns include: id (item ID), pcd2 (computed \(D^{2}\) value), N (number valid examinee responses per item). ipd_item numeric vector item indices flagged exhibiting item parameter drift (IPD), based specified critical value crit.val. items flagged crit.val = NULL, NULL. purify logical value indicating whether iterative purification procedure applied (TRUE) (FALSE). with_purify list containing results Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) analysis applying purification procedure. list populated purify = TRUE crit.val NULL. includes: ipd_stat data frame reporting final Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistics purification. Columns include: id (item ID), pcd2 (computed \(D^{2}\) value), N (number valid responses), n.iter (iteration number item evaluated). ipd_item numeric vector item indices flagged IPD items purification. Items ordered iteration flagged. n.iter integer indicating number purification iterations completed. complete logical value indicating whether purification procedure converged reaching maximum number iterations (max.iter). FALSE, iteration limit reached convergence. crit.val numeric value indicating critical threshold used flag items parameter drift. specified user, NULL.

title: Pseudo-count D2 method — pcd2
text: Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistic quantifies item parameter drift (IPD) computing weighted squared differences observed expected response frequencies score category across ability levels. expected frequencies determined using posterior distribution examinee's ability (Stone, 2000). Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistic calculated : $$ Pseudo-count D^{2} = \sum_{k=1}^{Q} \left( \frac{r_{0k} + r_{1k}}{N}\right) \left( \frac{r_{1k}}{r_{0k} + r_{1k}} - E_{1k} \right)^2 $$ \(r_{0k}\) \(r_{1k}\) pseudo-counts incorrect correct responses ability level \(k\), \(E_{1k}\) expected proportion correct responses ability level \(k\), calculated using item parameters item bank, \(N\) total count examinees received item. Critical Value (crit.val): crit.val argument specifies threshold used flag item exhibiting potential parameter drift. item's Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) value exceeds threshold, identified drifted item. crit.val = NULL, function reports raw statistic without flagging. Minimum Response Count (min.resp): min.resp argument sets lower bound number responses required item included analysis. Items fewer responses min.resp automatically excluded replacing responses NA. avoids unreliable estimates based small sample sizes. Purification Procedure: Although Cappaert et al. (2018) incorporate purification method, pcd2() implements optional iterative purification process similar Lim et al. (2022). purify = TRUE crit.val provided: procedure begins identifying items flagged drift using initial Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) statistics. subsequent iteration, item highest flagged Pseudo-count \(D^{2}\) value removed item set, statistics recalculated using remaining items. process continues additional items flagged number iterations reaches max.iter. flagged items statistics saved, convergence status reported. process ensures drift detection distorted already-flagged items, improving robustness results.

title: Pseudo-count D2 method — pcd2
text: Cappaert, K. J., Wen, Y., & Chang, Y. F. (2018). Evaluating CAT-adjusted approaches suspected item parameter drift detection. Measurement: Interdisciplinary Research Perspectives, 16(4), 226-238. Stone, C. . (2000). Monte Carlo based null distribution alternative goodness--fit test statistic IRT models. Journal educational measurement, 37(1), 58-75.

## ## The Pseudo-count D2 statistic has no closed-form null distribution. ## Following Lim & Han (in press), the critical value is estimated empirically ## via bootstrap: ##   (1) Select drift-free (anchor) items to form the null D2 distribution. ##   (2) Repeatedly resample from those values and take the 95th percentile. ##   (3) Average across bootstrap iterations to obtain the critical value. ## ## The simIPD dataset provides: ##   item_par  : original 360-item pool (3PLM, irtQ format) ##   foc_resp  : focal group CAT responses (N = 3,000; TL = 30; ~92% NA) ##   key_item  : indices of 90 highly-exposed key items (IPD analysis targets) ##   item.skip : indices of 270 non-key items (excluded from analysis) ##   ipd_item  : 18 truly drifted items (ground truth; a & b each -0.5) ## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------  data(simIPD)  ## -- Step 1. Select anchor items for bootstrap ----------------------------- ## From the full item pool, select items that (a) have sufficient observed ## responses (>= boot_size) and (b) are not known IPD items. These items ## serve as the empirical null distribution of D2. ## boot_size = 300: chosen to match the minimum response count used in the ##   bootstrap procedure of the simulation study (Lim & Han, in press). ## In practice, exclude items you know or suspect have drifted; here the ## ground truth (simIPD$ipd_item) is used for illustration. boot_size    <- 300 n_resp       <- colSums(!is.na(simIPD$foc_resp))   # observed responses per item anchor_items <- setdiff(which(n_resp >= boot_size), simIPD$ipd_item)  ## -- Step 2. Compute null D2 values for the anchor items ------------------ pcd2_null <- pcd2(   x        = simIPD$item_par[anchor_items, ],   data     = simIPD$foc_resp[, anchor_items],   D        = 1.7,   crit.val = NULL,   purify   = FALSE )$no_purify$ipd_stat$pcd2  ## -- Step 3. Bootstrap critical value (Lim & Han, in press) -------------- ## For each bootstrap iteration: resample boot_size D2 values from the null ## distribution and take the 95th percentile. The critical value is the mean ## of these percentiles across all iterations. ## n_boots = 500: reduced for demo speed; use 10,000 in practice for a ##   stable critical value estimate. set.seed(2024) n_boots <- 500  crit_val <- purrr::map_dbl(   .x = 1:n_boots,   .f = ~ sample(x = pcd2_null, size = boot_size, replace = TRUE) |>            stats::quantile(probs = 0.95) ) |> mean()  cat("Bootstrap critical value (alpha = 0.05):", round(crit_val, 6), "
") #> Bootstrap critical value (alpha = 0.05): 0.003013   ## -- Step 4. Run PCD2 with the bootstrap critical value + purification -- pcd2_result <- pcd2(   x         = simIPD$item_par,   data      = simIPD$foc_resp,   D         = 1.7,   item.skip = simIPD$item.skip,   crit.val  = crit_val,   purify    = TRUE,   max.iter  = 30 ) #> Warning: Item(s) 17, Item(s) 19, Item(s) 22, Item(s) 24, Item(s) 27, Item(s) 30, Item(s) 32, Item(s) 34, Item(s) 44, Item(s) 47, Item(s) 50, Item(s) 54, Item(s) 56, Item(s) 65, Item(s) 73, Item(s) 76, Item(s) 77, Item(s) 82, Item(s) 86, Item(s) 93, Item(s) 102, Item(s) 105, Item(s) 108, Item(s) 111, Item(s) 112, Item(s) 120, Item(s) 122, Item(s) 131, Item(s) 137, Item(s) 140, Item(s) 144, Item(s) 155, Item(s) 156, Item(s) 164, Item(s) 165, Item(s) 174, Item(s) 176, Item(s) 182, Item(s) 193, Item(s) 196, Item(s) 201, Item(s) 206, Item(s) 219, Item(s) 222, Item(s) 223, Item(s) 225, Item(s) 232, Item(s) 241, Item(s) 255, Item(s) 265, Item(s) 269, Item(s) 271, Item(s) 278, Item(s) 279, Item(s) 284, Item(s) 286, Item(s) 289, Item(s) 291, Item(s) 292, Item(s) 293, Item(s) 295, Item(s) 305, Item(s) 313, Item(s) 315, Item(s) 316, Item(s) 339, Item(s) 342, Item(s) 343, Item(s) 344, Item(s) 345, Item(s) 352, Item(s) 353, Item(s) 359 has(have) no item response data.  #> Purification started...  #>   Iteration: 1  Iteration: 2  Iteration: 3  Iteration: 4  Iteration: 5  Iteration: 6  Iteration: 7  Iteration: 8  Iteration: 9  Iteration: 10  Iteration: 11  Iteration: 12  Iteration: 13  Iteration: 14  Iteration: 15  Iteration: 16  Iteration: 17  Iteration: 18  Iteration: 19  Iteration: 20  #> Purification is finished.   ## -- Step 5. code: # \donttest{ ## --- RIPD Example: Detecting IPD in CAT --------------------------------- ## ## Background (Lim & Han, in press): ##   In CAT-based IPD detection using RIPD, the reference group is ##   "synthetic" -- created by re-administering a CAT to examinees whose ##   true abilities are set equal to the focal group's ML theta estimates, ##   using the ORIGINAL (pre-drift) item parameters. This eliminates the ##   need for recalibration and makes RIPD directly applicable to ##   operational CAT settings. ## ## The simIPD dataset contains: ##   - foc_resp / foc_score : focal group CAT responses + ML theta estimates ##                            (IPD items: a and b each drifted by -0.5) ##   - ref_resp / ref_score : synthetic reference group CAT responses + ML ##                            theta estimates (original parameters, 1F size) ##   - item_par  : original (non-drifted) 360-item pool in irtQ format ##   - key_item  : indices of 90 key items (highly exposed in CAT) ##   - item.skip : indices of 270 non-key items (excluded from RIPD) ##   - ipd_item  : indices of 18 truly drifted items (ground truth) ## -------------------------------------------------------------------------  data(simIPD)  ## Step 1. Combine focal and synthetic reference group data ##         (reference group first, then focal group -- as in the paper) data  <- rbind(simIPD$ref_resp,  simIPD$foc_resp) score <- c(simIPD$ref_score,     simIPD$foc_score) group <- c(rep(0, nrow(simIPD$ref_resp)),   # 0 = reference            rep(1, nrow(simIPD$foc_resp)))   # 1 = focal  ## Step 2. Run RIPD with purification (recommended statistic: RIPD_RS) ##         item.skip excludes the 270 non-key items from analysis ripd_result <- ripd(   x          = simIPD$item_par,   data       = data,   score      = score,   group      = group,   focal.name = 1,           # focal group is coded as 1   item.skip  = simIPD$item.skip,   D          = 1.7,   alpha      = 0.05,   purify     = TRUE,   purify.by  = "ripdrs",    # purify using RIPD_RS (combined statistic)   max.iter   = 30,   method     = "ML",   range      = c(-5, 5) ) #> Purification started...  #>   Iteration: 1  Iteration: 2  Iteration: 3  Iteration: 4  Iteration: 5  Iteration: 6  Iteration: 7  Iteration: 8  Iteration: 9  Iteration: 10  Iteration: 11  Iteration: 12  Iteration: 13  Iteration: 14  Iteration: 15  Iteration: 16  Iteration: 17  Iteration: 18  Iteration: 19  Iteration: 20  #> Purification is finished.   ## Step 3. what: Run flexMIRT from Within R — run_flexmirt
title: Run flexMIRT from Within R — run_flexmirt
text: function runs flexMIRT (Cai, 2017) within R executing model specified flexMIRT syntax file (.e., *.flexmirt). use function, flexMIRT software must installed system. interface especially useful conducting simulation studies automating batch analyses involving flexMIRT.

title: Run flexMIRT from Within R — run_flexmirt
code: run_flexmirt(file.syntax, dir.flex = NULL, show.output.on.console = FALSE, ...)

title: Run flexMIRT from Within R — run_flexmirt
text: file.syntax single string character vector specifying path(s) one flexMIRT syntax files (extension *.flexmirt) executed. example: "C:/Users/Data/irtmodel.flexmirt". dir.flex character string specifying directory flexMIRT installed. folder name typically includes "flexMIRT" (e.g., "flexMIRT3", "flexMIRT 3.6"). set NULL, function searches flexMIRT "C:/Program Files" uses default path found (e.g., "C:/Program Files/flexMIRT3"). show.output..console Logical. TRUE, output system command printed R console. Default FALSE. See base::system(). ... Additional arguments passed base::system().

title: Run flexMIRT from Within R — run_flexmirt
text: Output files generated flexMIRT.

title: Run flexMIRT from Within R — run_flexmirt
text: using version flexMIRT earlier 3.6, directory specified dir.flex must contain following six files: WinFlexMIRT.exe FlexMIRT_x64.exe FlexMIRT_x86.exe vpg.dll vpg.licensing.client.dll vpg.licensing.dll flexMIRT version 3.6 later, directory must include following five files: WinFlexMIRT.exe vpg.dll vpg.licensing.client.dll vpg.licensing.dll VPGLicenseClientNet.dll along subdirectory named Resources contains following two files: flexMIRT_x64_AVX.exe flexMIRT_x86_AVX.exe

title: Multistage-Adaptive Test (MST) Simulation — run_mst
text: Simulates MST administration panel examinees. stage, examinees routed module based current ability estimate (set cut scores), final ability estimate computed accumulated responses across administered stages. function supports IRT models available irtQ (1PLM, 2PLM, 3PLM, GRM, GPCM) scoring methods available est_score. overall structure - separate route_score final_score list arguments, route_map/module matrix conventions - inspired randomMST() function mstR package (Magis et al., 2017).

title: Multistage-Adaptive Test (MST) Simulation — run_mst
text: x data frame item bank metadata following irtQ format (columns: id, cats, model, par.1, par.2, ...). Use shape_df create frame bring.flexmirt / bring.bilog / bring.parscale / bring.mirt import IRT software output. function calls confirm_df(x) internally validate normalise metadata. route_map binary square matrix defining MST transition structure. 1 row , column j means test taker can routed module module j. Equivalent transMatrix argument randomMST() mstR (Magis et al., 2017). See reval_mst details. module binary matrix mapping items (rows) modules (columns). module[j, m] = 1 means item j belongs module m. Equivalent modules argument randomMST() mstR (Magis et al., 2017). Must nrow(module) == nrow(x) ncol(module) == total number modules panel. theta numeric vector true ability values, one per examinee (length N). Used simulate item responses response NULL, stored result bias/RMSE computation. Either theta response () must provided. theta omitted response given, true.theta result NULL bias/RMSE computed. response optional N x J matrix observed item responses, N number examinees J total number items item bank (nrow(x)). Responses items administered given stage may NA. NULL theta provided, responses simulated internally via simdat. theta response provided, response used -theta retained evaluation (bias/RMSE computation) . Providing pre-generated response matrix (e.g., simdat(x, theta, D)) useful want compare different routing methods scoring options set item responses. D numeric scaling constant IRT model. Use D = 1 (default) logistic metric D = 1.702 approximate normal ogive. ini_mod Either NULL (default) single positive integer index stage-1 module list (panel_info(route_map)$config[[1]]). NULL, examinee independently randomly assigned one stage-1 modules equal probability — appropriate MST panels use spiralling booklet-based stage-1 assignment, panels single stage-1 module (random assignment equivalent fixed assignment). integer supplied, examinees begin stage-1 module; use ini_mod = 1 force examinees first (typically ) stage-1 module. route_method character string specifying adaptive routing method used select next module stage transition. "bmat" B-matching: selects module whose average item location (difficulty) closest current ability estimate. dichotomous items b parameter used; polytomous items (GRM, GPCM) mean threshold / step parameters used. "mfi" Maximum Fisher Information: selects module provides highest test information function (TIF) value current ability estimate. NULL Cut-score routing: uses cut scores supplied cut_score route examinees next module. examinee's current routing score compared cut scores determine reachable next-stage modules administer. Default "bmat". cut_score list numeric vectors specifying routing cut scores used route_method = NULL. list n.stage - 1 elements, one per stage transition. Element s contains cut scores routing stage s stage s+1. example, 1-3-3 MST, cut_score = list(c(-0.5,   0.5), c(-0.6, 0.6)) routes examinees whose stage-1 score \(-0.5\) easiest stage-2 module, \(-0.5\) \(0.5\) medium module, \(0.5\) hardest module. Ignored route_method "bmat" "mfi". Default NULL. route_score named list specifying scoring method options used obtain intermediate ability estimates routing decisions (applied every stage except last). Fields: method Character. One "ML" (maximum likelihood), "WL" (weighted likelihood; Warm, 1989), "MLF" (maximum likelihood fences; Han, 2016), "MAP" (maximum posteriori), "EAP" (expected posteriori; Bock & Mislevy, 1982), "EAP.SUM" (EAP summed scoring; Thissen et al., 1995), "INV.TCC" (inverse test characteristic curve scoring; Lim et al., 2021). "EAP.SUM" "INV.TCC", sum-score--theta lookup table pre-computed per module simulation loop; routing theta obtained single named-vector lookup, making approach efficient large \(N\). Default: "ML". range Numeric vector length 2: lower upper bounds ability scale. Default: c(-5, 5). norm.prior Numeric vector length 2: mean SD normal prior MAP/EAP. Default: c(0, 1). nquad Integer: number quadrature points EAP. Default: 41. tol Numeric: convergence tolerance iterative methods. Default: 1e-4. max.iter Integer: maximum iterations. Default: 100. fence.Numeric: discrimination parameter fence items MLF. Default: 3.0. fence.b Numeric vector length 2 NULL: difficulty parameters lower upper fence items. NULL, range used. Default: NULL. intpol Logical: enable linear interpolation "INV.TCC". Default: TRUE. range.tcc Numeric vector length 2: theta search range "INV.TCC". Default: c(-7, 7). max.Integer: maximum bisection iterations "INV.TCC". Default: 500L. Unspecified fields take defaults; full default list(method = "ML", range = c(-5, 5), norm.prior = c(0, 1), nquad = 41L, tol = 1e-4, max.iter = 100L, fence.= 3.0, fence.b = NULL, intpol = TRUE, range.tcc = c(-7, 7), max.= 500L). Example: route_score = list(method = "INV.TCC", range.tcc = c(-5, 5)). final_score named list specifying scoring method options final ability estimate (applied items accumulated across entire administered pathway). Supports fields route_score plus: method Character. Supports route_score methods, plus "EAP.SUM" (EAP summed scoring; Thissen et al., 1995) "INV.TCC" (inverse test characteristic curve scoring; Lim et al., 2021). Default: "ML". intpol Logical: enable linear interpolation "INV.TCC". Default: TRUE. range.tcc Numeric vector length 2: theta search range "INV.TCC". Default: c(-7, 7). max.Integer: maximum bisection iterations "INV.TCC". Default: 500. full default equivalent list(method = "ML", range = c(-5, 5), norm.prior = c(0, 1), nquad = 41L, tol = 1e-4, max.iter = 100L, fence.= 3.0, fence.b = NULL, intpol = TRUE, range.tcc = c(-7, 7), max.= 500L). se Logical. Whether compute return standard error final ability estimate. SE computed final_score methods: "ML", "WL", "MLF", "MAP", "EAP" via Fisher information / posterior variance; "EAP.SUM" "INV.TCC" via posterior standard deviation stored pre-computed lookup table. Returns NA se = FALSE, responses missing, sum score falls outside estimable range (e.g. perfect zero score beyond range.tcc). Default TRUE. missing scalar specifying missing (-administered) responses represented response. Default NA. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints progress messages console simulation (approximately every 10\ Default TRUE. return_full_resp Logical. TRUE, full.resp element returned list N x J integer matrix, N number examinees J = nrow(x) (items item bank). Cell [, j] contains examinee 's response item j item administered, NA . Row names "examinee.1", "examinee.2", etc.; column names item IDs x$id. FALSE (default), full.resp NULL. matrix can large large panels many examinees, populated default.

text: object class "run_mst", named list containing: call matched function call. est.theta numeric vector length N containing final ability estimate examinee. se.theta numeric vector length N containing standard error final ability estimate. seven final_score methods return SE; "EAP.SUM" "INV.TCC", SE posterior standard deviation pre-computed lookup table. NA se = FALSE, responses missing, sum score falls outside estimable range. theta.route N x n.stage numeric matrix ability estimates. Columns 1 n.stage - 1 intermediate routing estimates; column n.stage final estimate (equal est.theta). path N x n.stage integer matrix administered module indices. true.theta theta argument (true abilities), NULL provided. panel output panel_info(route_map). D scaling constant used. route.method route_method argument. route.score fully-merged route_score list (defaults applied). final.score fully-merged final_score list (defaults applied). N Number examinees. full.resp Always present returned list. return_full_resp = TRUE, N x J integer matrix item responses, N number examinees J = nrow(x) (total items item bank). Row names "examinee.1", "examinee.2", etc.; column names item IDs x$id. NA items administered given examinee. return_full_resp = FALSE (default), element NULL.

title: Multistage-Adaptive Test (MST) Simulation — run_mst
text: Panel structure: function first calls panel_info identify stages, module membership, valid pathways route_map. Module m's items module[, m] == 1. Response simulation: response NULL, item responses simulated theta using simdat. Stage-1 module assignment: ini_mod = NULL (default), examinee independently assigned stage-1 module uniform random sampling panel_info(route_map)$config[[1]]. panels single stage-1 module (common design), equivalent fixed assignment. panels multiple stage-1 modules (e.g., 2-3-3 3-2-3 design), random assignment approximates spiralling booklet-based allocation used operational testing. ini_mod integer, examinees start specified stage-1 module. Routing (stages 1 n.stage - 1): non-final stage, intermediate ability estimate obtained current stage's responses using route_score method. estimate used select next-stage module: "bmat": reachable module (via route_map) whose mean item location closest routing estimate selected. dichotomous items, location b parameter; GRM/GPCM items, mean threshold / step parameters. "mfi": reachable module highest test information routing estimate selected. NULL: routing estimate compared cut scores cut_score[[s]] (transition stage s stage s+1) assign rank, rank-th reachable module (ordered module index) administered. rank exceeds number reachable modules, last module used. Final scoring: Responses administered stages concatenated, final ability estimate computed using final_score method.

text: named list eight elements: item_par data frame 360 rows 6 columns containing original (pre-drift) item parameters irtQ format (columns: id, cats, model, par.1, par.2, par.3).  items follow 3PLM. key_item integer vector length 90 giving row indices (item_par) key items — items selected preliminary CAT simulation highly exposed therefore relevant IPD analysis. item.skip integer vector length 270 giving row indices non-key items excluded RIPD analysis (.e., complement key_item 1:360). Pass vector item.skip argument ripd(). ipd_item integer vector length 18 giving row indices items subjected IPD manipulation.  18 items (5% 360-item pool) discrimination () difficulty (b) parameters decreased 0.5.  18 items members key_item. foc_resp integer matrix dimensions 3000 × 360 containing focal group CAT response data.  row one examinee; column corresponds item item_par.  CAT administers 30 items per examinee, approximately 92% entries NA.  Responses generated using drifted item parameters (focal examinees exposed IPD items; exposure rate = 100%). foc_score numeric vector length 3000 containing focal group final maximum likelihood (ML) theta estimates obtained CAT. ref_resp integer matrix dimensions 3000 × 360 containing synthetic reference group CAT response data (sparsity structure foc_resp).  reference group constructed : (1) using foc_score true ability values (1F scaling, .e., reference group size focal group); (2) generating item responses original (non-drifted) item parameters; (3) running independent CAT simulation. synthetic reference group mirrors construction described Lim & Han (press). ref_score numeric vector length 3000 containing synthetic reference group final ML theta estimates.

title: Simulated CAT Data for Item Parameter Drift (IPD) Detection — simIPD
text: Simulation conditions: Item pool: 360 three-parameter logistic model (3PLM) items Test length: 30 items per examinee Item selection: Maximum Fisher Information (MFI) target exposure rate 0.30 Focal group: \(n = 3{,}000\); true abilities drawn \(N(0, 1)\) Reference group: \(n = 3{,}000\) (1F); true abilities = foc_score IPD items: 18 (5% 360), randomly drawn key_item IPD manipulation: b decreased 0.50 Interim scoring: EAP; final scoring: ML Scaling constant: \(D = 1.7\) Random seed: 2024 Note reference group size: 1F reference group (size focal group) used compactness.  practice, larger synthetic reference groups (e.g., 3F–8F) recommended improve RIPD detection power (Lim & Han, press). larger reference group can created replicating focal theta estimates: e.g., rep(foc_score, times = 3) 3F group, re-running CAT simulation original item parameters.

Available IRT models : "1PLM", "2PLM", "3PLM", "DRM" dichotomous item data "GRM" "GPCM" polytomous item data Note "DRM" serves general label covering dichotomous IRT models (.e., "1PLM", "2PLM", "3PLM"), "GRM" "GPCM" represent graded response model (generalized) partial credit model, respectively. subsequent columns contain item parameters specified models. dichotomous items, fourth, fifth, sixth columns represent item discrimination (slope), item difficulty, item guessing parameters, respectively. Note GPCM item K unique score categories, K - 1 threshold parameters required, since threshold first category boundary always fixed 0. example, GPCM item five score categories, four threshold parameters must provided. example data frame single-format test shown : example data frame mixed-format test shown : See IRT Models section irtQ-package documentation details IRT models used irtQ package. convenient way create data frame argument x using function shape_df(). second approach simulate response data directly specifying item parameters, instead providing metadata data frame via x argument (see examples ). case, following arguments must also specified: theta, cats, pr.model, D. g.drm argument required simulating dichotomous item responses 3PL model. can omitted entirely dichotomous items follow 1PL 2PL model. However, test includes mixture 1PL, 2PL, 3PL items, g.drm vector must specified items, using NA non-3PL items. example, test consists four dichotomous items first two follow 3PL model third fourth follow 1PL 2PL models respectively, g.drm = c(0.2, 0.1, NA, NA) used. dichotomous items, element cats set 2. polytomous items, number unique score categories specified cats. simulating data mixed-format test, important specify cats correct item order. example, suppose responses simulated 10 examinees across 5 items, including 3 dichotomous items 2 polytomous items (3 categories), second fourth items polytomous. case, cats = c(2, 3, 2, 3, 2) used. title: S-X2 Fit Statistic — sx2_fit
text: Computes \(S\text{-}X^2\) item fit statistic proposed Orlando Thissen (2000, 2003). statistic evaluates fit IRT models comparing observed expected item response frequencies across summed score groups.

title: S-X2 Fit Statistic — sx2_fit
code: sx2_fit(x, ...)  # Default S3 method sx2_fit(   x,   data,   D = 1,   alpha = 0.05,   min.collapse = 1,   norm.prior = c(0, 1),   nquad = 30,   weights,   pcm.loc = NULL,   ... )  # S3 method for class 'est_item' sx2_fit(   x,   alpha = 0.05,   min.collapse = 1,   norm.prior = c(0, 1),   nquad = 30,   weights,   pcm.loc = NULL,   ... )  # S3 method for class 'est_irt' sx2_fit(   x,   alpha = 0.05,   min.collapse = 1,   norm.prior = c(0, 1),   nquad = 30,   weights,   pcm.loc = NULL,   ... )

title: S-X2 Fit Statistic — sx2_fit
text: x data frame containing item metadata (e.g., item parameters, number categories, IRT model types, etc.); object class est_irt obtained est_irt(), est_item est_item(). Additional arguments passed methods. data matrix examinees' item responses corresponding items specified x argument. Rows represent examinees columns represent items. D scaling constant used IRT models make logistic function closely approximate normal ogive function. value 1.7 commonly used purpose. Default 1. alpha numeric value specifying significance level (\(\alpha\)) hypothesis test associated \(S\text{-}X^2\) statistic. Default 0.05. min.collapse integer specifying minimum expected frequency required per cell adjacent cells collapsed. Default 1. See Details. norm.prior numeric vector length two specifying mean standard deviation normal prior distribution. values used generate Gaussian quadrature points weights. Ignored method "ML", "MLF", "WL", "INV.TCC". Default c(0, 1). nquad integer specifying number Gaussian quadrature points used approximate normal prior distribution. Default 30. weights two-column matrix data frame containing quadrature points (first column) corresponding weights (second column) latent ability distribution. omitted, default values generated using gen.weight() according norm.prior nquad arguments. pcm.loc optional integer vector indicating row indices items follow partial credit model (PCM), slope parameters fixed. Default NULL.

title: S-X2 Fit Statistic — sx2_fit
text: accuracy \(\chi^{2}\) approximation item fit statistics can compromised expected cell frequencies contingency tables small (Orlando & Thissen, 2000). address issue, Orlando Thissen (2000) proposed collapsing adjacent summed score groups ensure minimum expected frequency least 1. However, applying collapsing approach directly polytomous item data can result excessive information loss (Kang & Chen, 2008). mitigate , Kang Chen (2008) instead collapsed adjacent response categories within summed score group, maintaining minimum expected frequency 1 per category. collapsing strategies implemented sx2_fit(). different minimum expected frequency desired, can specified via min.collapse argument. item labeled "DRM" item metadata, treated 3PLM item computing degrees freedom \(S\text{-}X^2\) statistic. Additionally, missing responses data automatically replaced incorrect responses (.e., 0s).

title: Write a
text: x data frame item metadata (e.g., item parameters, number categories, model types) single group, list data frames multiple groups. See est_irt() simdat() item metadata format. can also create metadata using shape_df(). file character string specifying destination file path (".txt" extension). norm.pop numeric vector length two specifying mean standard deviation normal population ability distribution single group, list vectors multiple groups. list provided, internal vector must contain mean standard deviation group's ability distribution (e.g., norm.pop = list(c(0, 1), c(0, 0.8), c(0.5, 1.2)) three groups). mgroup = TRUE single vector provided (e.g., norm.pop = c(0, 1)), recycled across groups. default c(0, 1). rePar logical value indicating whether item parameters reparameterized. TRUE, item intercepts logits guessing parameters assumed. FALSE, item difficulty guessing parameters assumed. mgroup logical value indicating whether file includes multiple groups. code: # \donttest{ ## 1. Create a "-prm.txt" file for a single group ##    using the simulated CAT data # 1-(1) Extract the item metadata x <- simCAT_MX$item.prm  # 1-(2) Set the name of the "-prm.txt" file temp_prm <- file.path(tempdir(), "single_group_temp-prm.txt")  # 1-(3) Write the "-prm.txt" file write.flexmirt(x, file = temp_prm, norm.pop = c(0, 1), rePar = FALSE)  ## 2. Create a "-prm.txt" file for multiple groups ##    using simulated multi-group data # 2-(1) Extract the item metadata x <- simMG$item.prm  # Set the name of the "-prm.txt" file temp_prm <- file.path(tempdir(), "mg_group_temp-prm1.txt")  # Write the "-prm.txt" file write.flexmirt(x,   file = temp_prm, norm.pop = list(c(0, 1), c(0.5, 0.8), c(-0.3, 1.3)),   rePar = FALSE, mgroup = TRUE, group.name = c("GR1", "GR2", "GR3") )  # Or write the "-prm.txt" file so that # all groups share the same ability distribution # and group names are generated automatically temp_prm <- file.path(tempdir(), "mg_group_temp-prm2.txt") write.flexmirt(x,   file = temp_prm, norm.pop = c(0, 1),   rePar = FALSE, mgroup = TRUE, group.name = NULL ) # }

title: irtQ 1.2.0
text: Added new function, find_cut(), identifies TIF-crossing routing cut scores MST panels. adjacent module pair within stage, function locates theta two modules’ test information functions (TIFs) intersect. warning issued mean difficulty order modules within stage differs input index order. Added new S3 method, plot.find_cut(), visualizes TIF curves routing cut scores stage stage using ggplot2 facets. Proper, anomalous, unselected cut scores distinguished line type. layout argument ("vertical" / "horizontal") controls facet orientation. Added new function, run_mst(), simulates MST administrations given panel structure returns response data along ability routing information simulated examinee. Added new exported dataset, simIPD, contains simulated CAT response data illustrating IPD detection ripd() pcd2(). dataset represents one replication CAT simulation (N = 3,000; test length = 30; 360-item 3PLM pool) 5% items (18 items) aa bb parameters decreased 0.5.

title: irtQ 1.2.0
text: est_irt(), est_item(), est_mg() now accept partial control list. Users can specify arguments wish override (e.g., control = list(iter.max = 500)); unspecified arguments fall back defaults via modifyList(). Reorganized pkgdown reference page: ripd() pcd2() now grouped new Item Parameter Drift (IPD) section, reval_mst(), panel_info(), find_cut(), plot.find_cut(), run_mst() grouped new Multistage-Adaptive Test (MST) section.

title: irtQ 1.2.0
text: Expanded documentation ripd() adding @details section covers theoretical background RIPD framework, asymptotic distributions three RIPD statistics, drift-type diagnostic guide, CAT-specific three-step workflow, purification procedure. Also added \donttest{} example demonstrating complete CAT-based IPD detection workflow using simIPD dataset. Updated @references include Lim & Choe (2023) replaced previous conference paper citation -press journal reference (Lim & Han, press). Added \donttest{} example pcd2() demonstrating CAT-based IPD detection using simIPD dataset, including bootstrap critical value procedure described Lim & Han (press).

title: irtQ 1.1.0
text: Improved speed reduced memory usage item parameter estimation standard error computation est_irt(), est_item(), est_mg(). Improved computational speed est_score() 52% dichotomous items (N = 10,000) 27% mixed-format tests, series optimizations. Improved computational speed sx2_fit() substantially replacing O(J²) Lord-Wingersky recursion forward-backward pass (11× faster mixed-format tests J = 55 items) vectorizing internal helper functions expFreq(), obsFreq(), PRM category-collapsing routine.

title: irtQ 1.1.0
text: Added unit test suite using testthat 3rd edition (testthat >= 3.0.0). Tests cover core functions including drm(), prm(), est_irt(), est_score(), est_mg(), rdif(), crdif(), catsib(), relevant tests across dichotomous, polytomous, mixed-format item scenarios (355 tests total). Added new function, ripd(), implements Residual-based Item Parameter Drift (RIPD) detection framework. function computes three RIPD statistics— RIPDRRIPD_R, RIPDSRIPD_S, RIPDRSRIPD_{RS}—item. RIPDRRIPD_R captures uniform item parameter drift (IPD) via differences mean raw residuals groups, RIPDSRIPD_S captures nonuniform IPD via differences mean squared residuals, RIPDRSRIPD_{RS} combined chi-square-based statistic sensitive types drift. optional purification procedure also supported.

title: irtQ 1.1.0
text: Getting Started irtQ: end--end overview package workflow. Item Parameter Estimation: detailed guidance est_irt(), est_item(), est_mg(). Ability Estimation: scoring methods available est_score(). Model-Data Fit Evaluation: using irtfit() sx2_fit() assess model fit. DIF Detection: applying rdif(), grdif(), catsib() detect item bias. Classification Accuracy Consistency: computing indices via cac_lee() cac_rud(). Utility Functions: usage info(), traceline(), lwrc(), simdat(), related helpers. Evaluating MST Panels reval_mst(): measurement precision bias evaluation multistage adaptive tests.

title: irtQ 1.1.0
text: Fixed minor bug sx2_fit() caused incorrect cell collapsing two adjacent score categories polytomous items computing S-X2X^2 item fit statistic. Fixed minor bugs est_score() info(). Resolved issue catsib() function failed responses missing (NA) either reference focal group. Updated cac_rud() include x argument, allowing users pass item metadata data frames directly. Revised default control parameters est_irt(), est_item(), est_mg(), updated documentation accordingly. Fixed minor bug est_score() function terms Newton-Raphson method. final bin exclusion step catsib_item() used hardcoded threshold 3 instead user-supplied min.binsize argument, causing inconsistent bin filtering behavior. reliability estimate rho2 catsib_one() clamped [0,1][0, 1], errvar > sigma2 (e.g., items purification cascade), negative rho2 reversed regression correction direction, inflating Type error rate. errvar >= sigma2 purification, rho2 collapsed 0, causing corrected scores converge group mean. group mean differences (impact), produced empty bin data frames invalid purification result. minimum floor 0.05 now enforced rho2 preserve score spread. Fixed critical bug covirt() guessing parameter (par[,3]) incorrectly passed difficulty parameter (par[,2]) integrand() function DRM items. caused gradient computation receive c = b, zeroed ∂P/∂\partial P/\partial ∂P/∂b\partial P/\partial b gradient components produced singular Fisher information matrix. Additionally, NA values par.3 1PLM 2PLM items now substituted 0 prior gradient evaluation prevent NA propagation.

title: irtQ 1.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2025-07-17 documentation irtQ package revised reflect updates function behavior, fix typos, provide relevant detailed information existing functions. new function, crdif(), added. function computes three statistics residual-based DIF detection framework using categorical residuals (RDIF-CR). allows detection global DIF, particularly polytomously scored items. new function, shape_df_fipc(), introduced. function merges fixed-item metadata automatically generated metadata new items produces single data frame ordered test position. designed support fixed item parameter calibration (FIPC) via est_irt() function. plot() method enhanced support display item characteristic curves given item single panel. pcd2() function updated include purification procedure. rdif() catsib() functions now include item.skip argument. allows users specify numeric vector item indices exclude DIF analysis.

title: irtQ 0.2.1
text: CRAN release: 2024-08-25 Enhanced functionality bind.fill() function adding new argument fill. value argument used fill missing data aligning datasets. Fixed bug within est_irt() function previously unable implement fixed item parameter calibration (FIPC) freely estimating single item given items fixed. Added new function, reval_mst(), evaluates measurement precision bias Multistage-Adaptive Test (MST) panels using recursion-based evaluation method introduced Lim et al. (2020). Added new function, pcd2(), computes Pseudo-count D2D^{2} statistics (Cappaert et al., 2018; Stone, 2000) detect item parameter drift.

title: irtQ 0.2.0
text: CRAN release: 2023-07-06 Introduced Warm’s (1989) Weighted Likelihood (WL) estimation method est_score() function. WL scoring method can now utilized setting method = "WL". Enhanced speed ability parameter estimation est_score() function using ML, MLF, MAP methods method argument. updated version performs approximately three times faster predecessor. Addressed bug within est_score() function previously unable accurately compute scores single item data provided. issue occurring EAP.SUM INV.TCC estimation methods. Added two new functions computing classification accuracy consistency: cac_rud() cac_lee(). cac_rud: function implements Rudner’s (2001, 2005) method computing classification accuracy consistency. takes cut scores, ability estimates, standard errors, optional weights inputs returns list containing confusion matrix, marginal conditional classification accuracy consistency indices, probability assigned level category, cut scores used analysis. cac_lee: function implements Lee’s (2010) method computing classification accuracy consistency. takes data frame containing item metadata, cut scores, optional ability estimates, optional weights, scaling factor, logical value indicating cut score metric inputs. returns list similar cac_rud. Added new function, llike_score(), computes loglikelihood ability parameters given item parameters response data. Enhanced functionality rdif() grdif() functions: now support graded response model (GRM) generalized partial credit model (GPCM). Fixed issue grdif() function inaccurately calculated GRDIF statistics group membership specified non-standard way. Specifically, problem arose 0 wasn’t used reference group consecutive numbers (e.g., 1, 2, 3) weren’t used represent focal groups group argument.
